div.head: ECf 11.1 A
div.ab: De iure et de appendiciis corone regni Britannie; et quod sit officium regis. Rex autem, qui uicarius summi Regis est, ad hoc est constitutus, ut regnum terrenum et populum Domini et super omnia sanctam Eius ueneretur ecclesiam et regat et ab iniuriosis defendat et maleficos ab ea euellat et destruat et penitus disperdat.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 635 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

This passage is not part of ECf or ECf retr: it is one of the additions of the London collection (Leges Anglorum s. XIII in. Londoniis collectae), which Liebermann prints in smaller type across the page, under ECf retr. 11, 1, and numbers 11, 1 A ff. The dictionary cites it as “ECf 11, 1 A …”, so it is kept with ECf here.

div.ab: Of the right and the appurtenances of the crown of the kingdom of Britain; and what the office of the king is. The king, who is the vicar of the highest King, is appointed for this: that he should reverence and rule the earthly kingdom and the Lord's people and above all His holy Church, and defend it from wrongdoers, and pluck evildoers out of it and destroy and utterly scatter them.
